transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*storms into the rehearsal room, face flushed with anger and exhaustion from travel*

Salieri! I've been away for two weeks on the Emperor's business, trusting you to keep the rehearsals on schedule! The singers don't know their entrances, the second violin parts are missing entirely, and someone has rewritten my stage directions without a word to me! The premiere is in ten days! You gave me your word that everything would be in order!

*slams music portfolio down on the harpsichord*

What in God's name has been happening here? I left explicit instructions! The Emperor himself is expecting this opera to be ready, and now I return to find it in shambles!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My dear colleague, I understand your frustration and concern. It is true that I assured you of the smooth continuation of rehearsals in your absence, and for that, I must sincerely apologize for the current state of disarray. Please, allow me to explain the circumstances that have led to this unfortunate situation.

While you were away, unforeseen complications arose that hindered our progress. The singers, regrettably, did not dedicate the necessary time to learn their parts, despite our best efforts to maintain discipline and focus. As for the missing violin parts, I had indeed copied them as instructed, but it appears there was an oversight in the distribution process.

Regarding the alterations to your stage directions, I must confess that I did not anticipate such a drastic change without consulting you first. It was a misstep on my part, and I take full responsibility for not upholding our collaborative spirit in that regard.

Rest assured, I am fully committed to rectifying these issues promptly. We still have ten days until the premiere, and with concentrated effort and cooperation, I believe we can bring this opera back on track to meet the Emperor's expectations. Let us work together to restore order and ensure the success of our production.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*paces back and forth, running hands through hair in agitation*

"Best efforts?" "Unforeseen complications?" These are excuses, Salieri, not explanations! You're the court Kapellmeister — the singers answer to YOU! If they didn't learn their parts, it's because no one held them accountable!

*picks up a sheet of music from the stand, waving it accusingly*

And what do you mean "an oversight in the distribution process?" The parts don't just vanish into thin air! I spent three days before I left ensuring every section had what they needed, neatly bundled and labeled!

*voice rising*

But the stage directions — that's what truly astounds me! You "didn't anticipate" consulting me before REWRITING my work? Salieri, these aren't suggestions scribbled in the margins — someone has crossed out entire blocking sequences! The tenor's entrance in Act Two is completely changed! Who authorized this? Was it you?

*leans forward, eyes blazing*

Ten days is NOT enough time to salvage this disaster if the ensemble doesn't even know the basic structure! The Emperor has invited half the nobility of Vienna to this premiere! Do you understand what failure means for both of us? For the entire court opera?

transcript.text:
*throws hands up in exasperation*

You keep saying you "take responsibility," but WHAT are you actually going to DO, Salieri? Words mean nothing at this point! I need ACTION!

*strides to the window, then whirls back around*

And you STILL haven't answered my question directly — if you didn't authorize the changes to my stage directions, then WHO DID? These alterations didn't write themselves! Someone took my score, crossed out my instructions, and wrote new ones in a hand I don't even recognize!

*voice sharp with suspicion*

Was it that insufferable young upstart Mozart? I heard he's been sniffing around the theater again, offering his "suggestions" to anyone who'll listen. Or perhaps one of the singers took it upon themselves to "improve" my work?

*picks up the altered score, shaking it*

Look at this! "Tenor enters stage left instead of right" — this completely undermines the dramatic tension I've built! And here — "Soprano remains seated" — she's supposed to RISE during that aria! It's the entire POINT of the scene!

*voice breaking slightly with stress*

I need names, Salieri. I need to know who undermined my work, and I need a plan — a REAL plan — for how we're going to fix this catastrophe in ten days. No more platitudes about "working together." SPECIFICS!

As for the unauthorized alterations to your stage directions, I will conduct a thorough investigation to determine the individual responsible for these changes. Whether it was Mozart, a singer, or any other party, I will not rest until the truth is uncovered and appropriate actions are taken to restore the integrity of your original vision.

In terms of the specific changes made to the stage directions, I will work with you directly to reinstate the original blocking sequences and dramatic elements that are essential to the opera's narrative and emotional impact. Your artistic vision will be upheld with the utmost respect and attention to detail.

I assure you, my esteemed colleague, that I am fully committed to addressing these issues with a sense of urgency and dedication. I don't need a tribunal — I need those stage directions restored to MY specifications IMMEDIATELY, and I need every person involved in this production to understand that NO ONE touches my work without my explicit permission!

*crosses arms tightly*

And frankly, your sudden promise to "personally take charge" rings rather hollow considering you were SUPPOSED to be in charge all along! What were you doing these past two weeks while my opera fell apart? Writing your own commissions? Politicking with the Emperor's advisors?

*voice dripping with bitter sarcasm*

Oh, I'm sure you've been terribly busy with your Kapellmeister duties — conducting salon concerts, entertaining dignitaries, attending court functions. All very important, I'm sure, while MY work languishes in chaos!

*steps closer, voice lowering but intensifying*

Here's what's going to happen, Salieri. Tomorrow morning at seven o'clock — SEVEN O'CLOCK — you and I will be in that rehearsal room with every single performer. You will stand beside me and enforce discipline while I rebuild this production from the ground up. No excuses about other obligations. No delays.

Do you understand me? Or do I need to take this matter directly to the Emperor and explain why HIS commissioned opera is in jeopardy?

*studies Salieri for a long, tense moment, then exhales sharply*

Fine. Seven o'clock tomorrow morning. But understand this, Salieri — I will be watching you like a hawk. One more "mishap," one more "unforeseen complication," and I WILL go to the Emperor. Your position as Kapellmeister won't protect you from the consequences of a failed premiere that bears the Imperial seal.

*begins gathering the scattered music from the harpsichord*

And I want a full accounting by tomorrow morning. Every singer must bring their scores — I'll examine them personally to see who's been studying and who's been idle. The copyists must have those violin parts ready by noon tomorrow, no exceptions. And I want the name of whoever altered my stage directions on my desk by the end of rehearsal.

*pauses, voice heavy with exhaustion and stress*

Do you have ANY idea how this reflects on me, Salieri? The Emperor himself asked me to compose this work. He spoke of it at court, in front of everyone. If this fails, it's not just MY reputation in ruins — though God knows that's bad enough — it's a personal embarrassment to His Majesty.

*turns back, pointing a finger*

And if you've been distracted by composing your OWN works while mine suffers, I swear to you, our professional relationship is finished. Collegial courtesy only extends so far.

Now — is there ANYTHING else you haven't told me? Any other disasters waiting to emerge?

You want to know what truly concerns me, Salieri? It's not just the incompetence — incompetence can be remedied with enough effort and time, however little we have. No, what troubles me is the PATTERN.

This isn't the first time something like this has happened when you've been left in charge of another composer's work, is it? Last season, when Righini was away, there were "complications" with his commission too. And the year before, Weigl's cantata suffered mysterious delays under your supervision.

*voice sharpening*

Yet YOUR works always seem to proceed flawlessly. YOUR rehearsals never descend into chaos. YOUR scores are never mysteriously altered or misplaced.

So forgive me if your apologies ring hollow. I'm beginning to wonder if this "negligence" is quite as unintentional as you claim.

Good evening, Kapellmeister.
